Proposition: P1 Risk-correlated selection shifts experienced frequency; the sign is set by Cov(m, s)
Classification: Demonstrated (generic simulation and known-zero benchmark, positive-covariance calibration); derived analytically (Lemma 1)
Basis: selection ratio = 1 + Cov(m,s)/(E[m]E[s]); positive covariance yields selection_gap > 0 under endogenous observation at zero efficacy; adjusted hazard attenuation in the rainfall benchmark

Proposition: P2a Selection shifts experienced frequency proportionally; positive-covariance calibration
Basis: selection_ratio = p_ref/p_obj ≈ 1.71, analytically independent of baseline rarity under multiplicative state-dependent selection; ≈ 1.0 under exogenous observation; record term B_abs ≈ 0 on the observed support

Proposition: P2b Original hypothesis: rarity amplifies the absolute selection gap
Basis: absolute selection gap falls with rarity (≈ 0.72 × p_obj); the original rarity-amplification hypothesis for the frequency gap was driven by scaling of the composition effect with p, not by a rarity mechanism

Proposition: P2c Rarity changes the relative composition of modeled prices through nonlinear transformation and non-scaling reputation
Classification: Demonstrated (generic simulation); transformed term divergent analytically (Lemma 2)
Basis: D_rel(Model D) rises with rarity through both a nonlinear transformed-frequency part—the larger share in every simulated regime, asymptotically unbounded under Prelec weighting—and an additive reputation part whose share rises with rarity

Proposition: P3 Weighting moves the subjective layer relative to experience
Basis: B_subj differs across learner rules; selective memory exceeds experienced frequency

Proposition: P4 Model-implied quotes mix hazard and transformation
Basis: B_price and D_EV differ across pricing models A–D

Proposition: P5 Reputation decouples price from contemporaneous performance
Classification: Demonstrated (generic simulation; sharper in the known-zero benchmark)
Basis: Reputation premia coexist with small or negative contemporaneous price-success differences

Proposition: P6 Mean-performance equivalence limits inference from raw performance
Basis: Zero efficacy under endogenous observation reproduces the MEAN apparent success of positive efficacy under exogenous observation in the simulated rare regimes (first-moment only; regime-dependent, no solution in the common regime)
